strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#66851 (bug from edcbad30226d) by running pandas’ newly added regression tests around DatetimeIndex/Series dt accessors and isocalendar for years beyond int32 (including BC/negative years). The buggy revision produces wrapped/truncated year fields (and thus wrong day_of_year/ISO calendar), while the fixed revision raises ValueError for out-of-range years and returns correct Int32/UInt32 dtypes for isocalendar.

pinned_because: No version constraints are documented in the provided evidence for numpy/python-dateutil/cython, so versions cannot be reliably pinned from the context. NumPy is required for datetime64[M8[s]] support; pandas must be built from source because the bug is in pandas/_libs.tslibs.fields C-extension code paths.

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision edcbad30226d: the tests fail because year/isocalendar/day_of_year are computed from an int32-truncated/wrapped year (so the assertions expecting ValueError for dti.year/dt.year/dti.isocalendar, and expecting day_of_year==364/is_leap_year True, do not match). On fixed revision: the tests pass—dti[0].year returns the correct (out-of-range) year value, and accessing dti.year / Series(dti).dt.year / dti.isocalendar raises ValueError with the expected message; day_of_year and leap-year checks return 364 and True consistently.
strategy.numerical_probe: Trigger int32 truncation/wrap in datetime field accessors by using DatetimeIndex constructed from dtype='M8[s]' values whose year lies outside int32 range (very large positive years and very negative/BC years).
risks: This defect is specifically about how pandas writes/uses year fields as int32/unsigned inside pandas/_libs.tslibs.fields and related ccalendar helpers; the observed failures may depend on building pandas with its C extensions enabled (hence needs_build=true).

Because the evidence shows no documented NumPy version constraint, the exact behavior could vary across NumPy versions; however the bug is in pandas’ C-extension year handling, so choose a common supported NumPy (e.g., latest stable) and use the same environment for buggy vs fixed commits.

Some described wraparound examples involve isocalendar year being stored as unsigned (UInt32) before the fix; if the buggy revision doesn’t hit the unsigned-year path for your chosen test subset, you may need to run the additional regression test in pandas/tests/indexes/datetimes/methods/test_isocalendar.py::test_isocalendar_year_before_year_one.

If the test environment/platform can’t represent extremely large/small years in datetime64[s] construction, those specific parametrized values may fail earlier than the intended year-truncation assertion; on that platform, adjust by using other out-of-range years covered by the test that still successfully construct M8[s] values.
Architecture/toolchain differences (32-bit builds) could change int sizes and potentially mask or alter the truncation behavior; run on a standard 64-bit environment for a cleaner transition.

oracle.reference_source: Inferred from the provided diff and evidence: the regression tests assert exact dtype (Int32/UInt32) and exact behavior (ValueError raised with specific match, and exact day_of_year==364 / is_leap_year True).
oracle.why: The success criterion is the test outcome (assertion and exception matches) rather than separate numerical inspection.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The buggy revision does not consistently raise ValueError for out-of-range years and/or computes day_of_year/is_leap_year using a truncated/wrapped int32 year, so either the with pytest.raises blocks do not raise (or raise with a different message), and/or dti[0].day_of_year != 364 and dti[0].is_leap_year is False.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed revision correctly handles years outside int32: dti.year and Series(dti).dt.year raise ValueError with the expected message mentioning out-of-range int32 result; dti.isocalendar raises ValueError mentioning ISO year; day_of_year and is_leap_year return correct results (including leap-year status derived from the true year rather than a truncated year).
